definitions.definition: The potential difference across a conductor is directly proportional to the current in the conductor at constant temperature.
distractors: The potential difference across a conductor is inversely proportional to the current in the conductor.
The resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to the temperature.
The current in a conductor is directly proportional to its resistance.
The total voltage in a series circuit is equal to the sum of the individual voltage drops.
The power dissipated by a resistor is proportional to the square of the potential difference.
The resistance of a conductor is equal to the product of potential difference and current.

definitions.definition: A conductor that obeys Ohm's law (it has a constant resistance; its $V$ vs. $I$ graph is a straight line through the origin).
distractors: A conductor whose resistance increases as its temperature increases.
A conductor that only allows current to flow in one direction.
A conductor with zero internal resistance.
A component that stores electrical energy in a magnetic field.
A conductor that requires a specific threshold voltage before conducting.
A conductor whose $V$ vs. $I$ graph is a parabolic curve.

definitions.definition: A conductor that does not obey Ohm's law (resistance changes as temperature/current changes).
distractors: A conductor that obeys Ohm's law.
A conductor with an infinite resistance that does not allow current to pass.
A conductor whose $V$ vs. $I$ graph is a straight line passing through the origin.
A device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.
A power source with no internal resistance.
An ideal ammeter connected in series.

definitions.definition: The maximum energy provided by a battery per unit charge passing through it.
distractors: The force exerted on an electron as it moves through a conductor.
The total power dissipated by the external circuit.
The potential difference measured across the terminals of a battery when the switch is closed.
The opposition to the flow of charge within the battery itself.
The energy lost as heat per unit charge inside the cell.
The rate at which work is done by the battery.

definitions.definition: The potential difference measured across the terminals of a battery when charges are flowing through the circuit (switch closed).
distractors: The maximum energy provided by a battery per unit charge passing through it.
The total current flowing through the main branch of the circuit.
The potential difference across the internal resistance of the battery.
The reading on a voltmeter when the external circuit is disconnected.
The sum of all currents entering a junction.
The energy dissipated by the entire circuit over one hour.

definitions.definition: The opposition to the flow of charge within the battery itself.
distractors: The total equivalent resistance of the external circuit.
The resistance of the connecting wires in the circuit.
The force required to move a charge through a vacuum.
The potential difference across the battery when the switch is open.
The maximum current a battery can supply when short-circuited.
The sum of all resistors connected in parallel.

definitions.definition: The potential difference across the internal resistance of the battery when current flows, representing the energy lost as heat per unit charge inside the cell.
distractors: The potential difference measured across the external circuit.
The maximum voltage a battery can produce.
The voltage drop across an ideal ammeter.
The total energy provided by a battery per unit charge.
The voltage that is converted into useful mechanical work.
The reading on a voltmeter placed across an open switch.

proportionality.statement: If a resistor is added in parallel to an existing circuit, the total external resistance of the circuit will...
distractors: increase.
remain the same.
become zero.
double.
fluctuate depending on the internal resistance.
equal the value of the added resistor.

proportionality.statement: If a resistor is added in series to an existing circuit, the total external resistance of the circuit will...
distractors: decrease.
remain the same.
become zero.
halve.
fluctuate depending on the internal resistance.
equal the value of the added resistor.

proportionality.statement: In a circuit with internal resistance, if the total external resistance is decreased, the total current flowing from the battery will...
distractors: decrease.
remain the same.
become zero.
be unaffected by internal resistance.
fluctuate randomly.
halve.

proportionality.statement: In a circuit with internal resistance, if the total current drawn from the battery increases, the terminal potential difference ($V_{ext}$) will...
proportionality.correct: decrease, because the lost volts ($Ir$) increase.
distractors: increase, because the lost volts ($Ir$) decrease.
remain the same, because emf is constant.
increase, because the emf increases.
decrease, because the emf decreases.
become zero instantly.
remain constant, because internal resistance is constant.

concepts.question: A student measures the potential difference across a battery with the switch OPEN, and then again with the switch CLOSED. Which of the following is true?
concepts.correct: The reading is higher when the switch is OPEN, representing the emf.
distractors: The reading is lower when the switch is OPEN, representing the lost volts.
The reading is identical in both cases, representing the terminal voltage.
The reading is zero when the switch is OPEN.
The reading is higher when the switch is CLOSED, representing the emf.
The reading when CLOSED represents the internal resistance.
The reading when OPEN depends on the external resistance.

concepts.question: On a graph of Terminal Potential Difference ($V$) vs. Current ($I$) for a battery, what does the y-intercept represent?
concepts.correct: The electromotive force (emf) of the battery.
distractors: The internal resistance of the battery.
The total external resistance of the circuit.
The short-circuit current.
The lost volts.
The total power dissipated by the circuit.
The negative internal resistance.

concepts.question: On a graph of Terminal Potential Difference ($V$) vs. Current ($I$) for a battery, what does the negative of the gradient (slope) represent?
concepts.correct: The internal resistance ($r$) of the battery.
distractors: The electromotive force (emf) of the battery.
The total external resistance ($R_{ext}$).
The short-circuit current.
The lost volts.
The equivalent parallel resistance.
The total power of the battery.
